stem: A push or a pull acting on an object is called a __________.
solution: A force is a push or a pull that can change the state or shape of an object.

stem: A force can change the __________ of a moving object.
solution: A force can make an object move faster, slower, or change its direction of motion.

stem: A force applied on an object can also change its __________.
solution: A force can deform an object, changing its shape (e.g. squeezing dough).

stem: Forces that act only when two objects are in physical contact are called __________ forces.
solution: Contact forces, like muscular and friction forces, act only on touching objects.

stem: Forces that act without physical contact between objects are called __________ forces.
solution: Non-contact forces such as gravity, magnetic and electrostatic forces act at a distance.

stem: The force exerted by our muscles is an example of a __________ force.
solution: Muscular force is a contact force applied by the action of muscles.

stem: The force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact is called __________.
solution: Friction acts between surfaces in contact and opposes their relative motion.

stem: Friction always acts in a direction __________ to the motion of an object.
solution: Friction opposes motion, so it acts in the direction opposite to the object's movement.

stem: Friction is greater on a __________ surface.
solution: Rough surfaces produce more friction than smooth ones.

stem: Which of the following is a way to reduce friction?
solution: Lubricants such as oil reduce friction between surfaces.

stem: The treads (grooves) on tyres and shoe soles are made to __________.
solution: Treads increase friction, giving better grip and preventing slipping.

stem: Ball bearings are used in machines to __________.
options: reduce friction by converting sliding into rolling
solution: Ball bearings replace sliding with rolling, greatly reducing friction.

stem: Rolling friction is generally __________ than sliding friction.
solution: Rolling friction is much less than sliding friction, which is why wheels ease movement.

stem: The force of attraction between any two objects due to their mass is called __________.
solution: Gravitational force is the attraction between objects because of their masses.

stem: The force with which the Earth pulls objects towards its centre is called __________.
solution: Gravity is the Earth's gravitational pull on objects towards its centre.

stem: An object thrown up comes back down because of __________.
solution: Earth's gravity pulls the object back down towards the ground.

stem: The weight of an object is the __________ acting on it.
solution: Weight is the gravitational force with which the Earth attracts an object.

stem: Two magnets brought together can exert force __________ contact.
solution: Magnetic force is a non-contact force, acting between magnets without touching.

stem: Like poles of two magnets __________ each other.
solution: Like poles (N–N or S–S) repel each other.

stem: Unlike poles of two magnets __________ each other.
solution: Unlike poles (N–S) attract each other.

stem: The force between charged objects, such as a rubbed comb attracting bits of paper, is called __________ force.
solution: Electrostatic force acts between electric charges and is a non-contact force.

stem: When two or more forces act on an object in the same direction, the net force is their __________.
solution: Forces in the same direction add up to give a larger net force.

stem: When two forces act on an object in opposite directions, the net force is their __________.
solution: Opposing forces subtract; the net force is their difference in the direction of the larger.

stem: If two equal and opposite forces act on an object, the net force is __________.
solution: Equal and opposite forces cancel out, giving zero net force.

stem: The upward force exerted by a liquid on an object placed in it is called __________.
solution: Buoyant force, or upthrust, is the upward force a fluid exerts on an immersed object.

stem: An object floats in a liquid when the buoyant force is __________ its weight.
solution: An object floats when the upthrust balances or exceeds its weight.

stem: A stone sinks in water because its weight is __________ the buoyant force.
solution: When weight exceeds the upthrust, the object sinks.

stem: Objects feel lighter in water because of the __________ force.
solution: The upward buoyant force partly supports the object, making it feel lighter in water.

stem: The resistance offered by air to a moving object is called __________.
solution: Air resistance is a form of friction that opposes motion through air.

stem: A parachute works by increasing __________ to slow the fall.
solution: The large parachute increases air resistance, slowing the descent.

stem: Streamlined shapes of birds, fish and aircraft help to __________.
options: reduce resistance from air or water
solution: Streamlining reduces the resistance of air or water, allowing easier, faster movement.

stem: Friction produces __________ when two surfaces rub together.
solution: Rubbing surfaces produces heat, which is why our palms warm when rubbed together.

stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of friction?
options: Wear and tear of machine parts
solution: Friction wears out machine parts and wastes energy as heat, a disadvantage.

stem: Which of the following is an advantage of friction?
options: It enables us to walk without slipping
solution: Friction lets us walk, grip and stop; without it walking would be impossible.

stem: The force needed to just start moving an object at rest is related to __________ friction.
solution: Static friction acts on a stationary object and must be overcome to start motion.

stem: Once an object is moving, the friction acting on it is called __________ friction.
solution: Sliding (kinetic) friction acts on an object that is already moving.

stem: Sliding friction is usually __________ than static friction.
solution: Once motion begins, sliding friction is a little less than the static friction needed to start it.

stem: A spring balance measures force using the fact that the spring __________ under a force.
options: stretches by an amount related to the force
solution: A spring stretches in proportion to the force, allowing the balance to measure it.

stem: The SI unit of force is the __________.
solution: Force is measured in newtons (N) in SI units.

stem: The interaction between a magnet and an iron nail placed a short distance apart shows that magnetic force can act __________.
solution: The nail is attracted before touching, showing magnetic force acts at a distance.

stem: A charged balloon sticks to a wall due to __________ force.
solution: The charge on the balloon induces an opposite charge on the wall, and electrostatic attraction holds it.

stem: The heavier an object, the __________ the gravitational force with which the Earth pulls it.
solution: Gravitational force (weight) increases with the mass of the object.

stem: Applying oil to a squeaky door hinge reduces the __________ between the moving parts.
solution: Oil acts as a lubricant, reducing friction and the squeak.

stem: The effect of a force depends on its __________ as well as the direction in which it acts.
solution: A force is described by both its magnitude and its direction.

stem: Pressing a lump of clay into a new shape shows that a force can __________.
options: change the shape of an object
solution: Applying force to clay deforms it, changing its shape.

stem: Which of the following pairs are both non-contact forces?
solution: Gravitational and magnetic forces both act without contact.

stem: A boat floats while a nail sinks in water mainly because of the difference in their __________.
solution: The boat's overall density (with air) is less than water, so it floats, while the dense nail sinks.

stem: Sportspeople wear spiked shoes to __________ on the ground.
solution: Spikes dig in and increase friction, giving a firm grip so runners do not slip.

stem: The direction of the buoyant force on a submerged object is always __________.
solution: The buoyant force always acts upward on an object immersed in a fluid.

stem: When you rub an inflated balloon on your hair, the balloon acquires the ability to attract small paper bits due to __________.
solution: Rubbing transfers charge, giving the balloon a static charge that attracts light objects electrostatically.
